data.hypothesis: For positive target masses, accumulating acceleration directly cancels the per-pair target-mass factor and the final division by target mass. Computing softened reciprocal-distance-cubed with rsqrtf and two multiplies may also reduce per-pair arithmetic. Correctness, especially for extreme masses, must be established by the oracle before any timing comparison.
data.notes: This is a proposed candidate only; no validation or timing was run here. It retains the softening, self-interaction skip, direct source loads, baseline target mapping, Euler update order, and unchanged mass copy. Require oracle/tolerance checks—including coincident particles, extreme masses, and distributed large rows—before comparing official timings. The baseline was correct with three reported timing repetitions averaging 0.0018452863847980042 seconds; that is not a measurement of this candidate.
transformations: Accumulate per-target acceleration directly, using cancellation of the positive target mass instead of accumulating force and dividing afterward.
Replace sqrtf plus division by an explicit rsqrtf-based softened reciprocal-distance-cubed calculation.
Retain the direct source loads, target mapping, self-skip, softened distance, Euler update sequence, and exact mass copy.
